nodes.Name: stackpool
nodes.DocComment:
Global pool of spans that have free stacks.
Stacks are assigned an order according to size.

	order = log_2(size/FixedStack)

There is a free list for each order.

nodes.Name: stackLarge
nodes.DocComment: Global pool of large stack spans.

nodes.Name: stacklog2
nodes.DocComment: stacklog2 returns ⌊log_2(n)⌋.

nodes.Name: stackpoolalloc
nodes.DocComment:
Allocates a stack from the free pool. Must be called with
stackpool[order].item.mu held.

nodes.Name: stackpoolfree
nodes.DocComment: Adds stack x to the free pool. Must be called with stackpool[order].item.mu held.

nodes.Name: stackcacherefill
nodes.DocComment:
stackcacherefill/stackcacherelease implement a global pool of stack segments.
The pool is required to prevent unlimited growth of per-thread caches.

go:systemstack

nodes.Name: stackcacherelease
nodes.DocComment: go:systemstack

nodes.Name: stackcache_clear
nodes.DocComment: go:systemstack

nodes.Name: stackalloc
nodes.DocComment:
stackalloc allocates an n byte stack.

stackalloc must run on the system stack because it uses per-P
resources and must not split the stack.

go:systemstack

nodes.Name: stackfree
nodes.DocComment:
stackfree frees an n byte stack allocation at stk.

stackfree must run on the system stack because it uses per-P
resources and must not split the stack.

go:systemstack

Fields.Name: delta
Fields.DocComment: ptr distance from old to new stack (newbase - oldbase)

nodes.Name: adjustpointer
nodes.DocComment:
adjustpointer checks whether *vpp is in the old stack described by adjinfo.
If so, it rewrites *vpp to point into the new stack.

nodes.Name: bitvector
nodes.DocComment:
Information from the compiler about the layout of stack frames.
Note: this type must agree with reflect.bitVector.

nodes.Name: ptrbit
nodes.DocComment:
ptrbit returns the i'th bit in bv.
ptrbit is less efficient than iterating directly over bitvector bits,
and should only be used in non-performance-critical code.
See adjustpointers for an example of a high-efficiency walk of a bitvector.

nodes.Name: adjustpointers
nodes.DocComment:
bv describes the memory starting at address scanp.
Adjust any pointers contained therein.

nodes.Name: adjustframe
nodes.DocComment: Note: the argument/return area is adjusted by the callee.

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: stk.lo <= p && p < stk.hi && p > sghi

nodes.Name: syncadjustsudogs
nodes.DocComment:
syncadjustsudogs adjusts gp's sudogs and copies the part of gp's
stack they refer to while synchronizing with concurrent channel
operations. It returns the number of bytes of stack copied.

nodes.Name: copystack
nodes.DocComment:
Copies gp's stack to a new stack of a different size.
Caller must have changed gp status to Gcopystack.

nodes.Name: round2
nodes.DocComment: round x up to a power of 2.

nodes.Name: newstack
nodes.DocComment:
Called from runtime·morestack when more stack is needed.
Allocate larger stack and relocate to new stack.
Stack growth is multiplicative, for constant amortized cost.

g->atomicstatus will be Grunning or Gscanrunning upon entry.
If the scheduler is trying to stop this g, then it will set preemptStop.

This must be nowritebarrierrec because it can be called as part of
stack growth from other nowritebarrierrec functions, but the
compiler doesn't check this.

go:nowritebarrierrec

Children.Name: if
Children.RawSource: goarch.ArchFamily == goarch.AMD64 || goarch.ArchFamily == goarch.I386 || goarch.ArchFamily == goarch.WASM

nodes.Name: nilfunc
nodes.DocComment: go:nosplit

nodes.Name: gostartcallfn
nodes.DocComment:
adjust Gobuf as if it executed a call to fn
and then stopped before the first instruction in fn.

nodes.Name: isShrinkStackSafe
nodes.DocComment:
isShrinkStackSafe returns whether it's safe to attempt to shrink
gp's stack. Shrinking the stack is only safe when we have precise
pointer maps for all frames on the stack. The caller must hold the
_Gscan bit for gp or must be running gp itself.

nodes.Name: shrinkstack
nodes.DocComment:
Maybe shrink the stack being used by gp.

gp must be stopped and we must own its stack. It may be in
_Grunning, but only if this is our own user G.

nodes.Name: freeStackSpans
nodes.DocComment: freeStackSpans frees unused stack spans at the end of GC.

nodes.Name: stackObjectRecord
nodes.DocComment:
A stackObjectRecord is generated by the compiler for each stack object in a stack frame.
This record must match the generator code in cmd/compile/internal/liveness/plive.go:emitStackObjects.

nodes.Name: gcdata
nodes.DocComment:
gcdata returns the number of bytes that contain pointers, and
a ptr/nonptr bitmask covering those bytes.
Note that this bitmask might be larger than internal/abi.MaxPtrmaskBytes.

nodes.Name: morestackc
nodes.DocComment:
This is exported as ABI0 via linkname so obj can call it.

go:nosplit
go:linkname morestackc

nodes.Name: startingStackSize
nodes.DocComment:
startingStackSize is the amount of stack that new goroutines start with.
It is a power of 2, and between fixedStack and maxstacksize, inclusive.
startingStackSize is updated every GC by tracking the average size of
stacks scanned during the GC.
